entry.title: Automating CERTRULE exception maintenance in S/4HANA for BTP apps
entry.content:
Introduction

In the previous blog I described how CERTRULE solves the problem of several e-mail addresses mapping to a single SAP user when BTP apps call the ABAP system with principal propagation. One rule covers everybody whose address is in SU01 and an exception list of explicit mappings covers the rest. That solution works. The effort to add the entries is cumbersome. When we moved from ECC to S/4HANA we had around 500 users to maintain as exceptions and it took our Basis colleagues more than 20 hours. This blog describes a much more efficient way to do it.

The two manual steps

Two steps have to be performed to maintain one entry in the exception list, typically Basis steps as they have the access to Cloud Connector and CERTRULE transaction in SAP.

  1. Open the Cloud Connector and generate a sample certificate with the e-mail address in the subject. 
  2. Open CERTRULE, import that certificate as an exception and assign the SAP user.

Screenshots to capture the steps:

Step one in the Cloud Connector. The subject pattern rule and the Create Sample Certificate action on its row.

The dialog asks for the e-mail address and generates the certificate.

Step two in CERTRULE (On SAP system). Import the certificate on the Explicit Mappings tab and assign the SAP user.

The certificate is read, CERTRULE shows the subject and the issuer, the status says the mapped e-mail does not exist, and the SAP user is required to be assigned. I'm adding default DEVELOPER SAP user in A4H.

One row in the exception list is created.

The work is in two systems (Cloud Connector and SAP), the certificate file is carried between them and a few minutes per address is required to add them.

Repeat for the next address. Both steps need a person with Cloud Connector administration and CERTRULE authorisations, which is why the work sits with Basis.

This makes it very time consuming. In our landscape, Basis team divided it amongst various Basis colleagues to make it possible to do it.

Questions on improving the process

To improve the process I investigated two things.

  1. Are both steps really essential.
  2. Can any of the steps be automated.

Initial automation thought

Initially I was thinking of a way to automate the generation of Cloud Connector certificates and then automate the import of the certificates in SAP. This will replicate the two stage process that we have to do manually.

However, I would not have admin access to the certificate via Cloud Connector keys to automate the generation of certificates. I gave up this approach as I realized it would not be possible.

I then changed my approach to investigate what SAP does when a certificate is imported in SAP. My theory was that the certificate is not technically essential. SAP is able to use certificate attributes to add the explicit mappings.

The first half covers the ABAP side: what CERTRULE actually stores, what the standard code behind the transaction does, which tables and APIs are involved and the issue I found around hashes.

The second half is the BTP side to make the solution work: A simple BTP app that reads a CSV file and calls a custom HTTP handler on SAP system to update the explicit mappings.

Landscape used for the test

The test ran on a local ABAP Platform trial in Docker with the Cloud Connector that comes with it. The BTP side is a trial subaccount on Cloud Foundry with a destination of proxy type OnPremise and authentication PrincipalPropagation. The identity provider is an Identity Authentication tenant.

The Cloud Connector issues a short lived certificate for every call from BTP with the subject CN=e-mail address,O=POC,C=AU and its own CA as issuer. CERTRULE maps the CN to the SU01 address with one rule. Every address that is not in SU01 needs an explicit mapping.

 

The browser knows an e-mail address. The token from XSUAA carries it. The Cloud Connector turns it into a certificate. CERTRULE turns the certificate into an SAP user. Only then does any ABAP code run. Nothing on the BTP side ever knows an SAP user name.

Step 1. Is the certificate essential

The first question was whether the certificate from the Cloud Connector is needed at all. The way to answer it is to see what CERTRULE does with it, so I debugged the standard code behind the transaction and traced what it reads and writes.

The explicit mappings tab in CERTRULE shows subject, issuer, user, creation date and creator. The old mapping table USREXTID has no creation date so the data cannot be there. SQL trace in ST05 while opening the tab shows the table. It is USRCERTMAP and it is read by class CL_CERTRULE_EXCEPTIONS in package SUSR_CERT.

The table has eight fields. The two key fields SUBJECTH and ISSUERH are hashes. The subject and the issuer are stored as text next to them but the key is the hash. That rules out a direct insert and it rules out SM30.

Step 2. The API behind the dialog

The import in the dialog reads the subject and the issuer off the certificate and hands those two strings to the SU01 identity framework. The certificate is only the carrier. Generating it in the Cloud Connector is required by the dialog to derive the attributes that end up in the SAP tables, but the certificate itself is not technically essential. That answers the first question and it opens the second one, because two strings can come from a file.

Class CL_CERTRULE_MIGRATION_UI proved useful in understanding this. That class shows how SAP itself creates a mapping without a certificate. It retrieves the users through the identity factory and adds a mapping with subject and issuer as strings.

cl_identity_factory=>retrieve_for_update(
  EXPORTING it_bname      = lt_bname
  IMPORTING et_node_root  = lt_identity
            eo_msg_buffer = lo_msg ).

ls_certmap-subject     = lv_subject.
ls_certmap-issuer      = lv_issuer.
ls_certmap-change_mode = 'I'.
lr_identity->idref->if_identity_certmap~add_certmap(
  EXPORTING is_certmap    = ls_certmap
  IMPORTING eo_msg_buffer = lo_msg ).

cl_identity_factory=>do_check( IMPORTING eo_msg_buffer = lo_msg ev_rejected = lv_rejected ).
cl_identity_factory=>do_save( EXPORTING iv_update_task = abap_false
                              IMPORTING eo_msg_buffer = lo_msg ev_rejected = lv_rejected ).
COMMIT WORK AND WAIT.
cl_identity_factory=>cleanup( it_bname = lt_bname ).

The structure SUID_ST_NODE_CERTMAP has the hash fields and the string fields. The caller fills the strings and the framework computes the hashes on save. That is the whole trick. The certificate in the dialog is only there to read the two strings off it.

Step 3. It still didn't work

The first version passed the strings exactly as the explicit mappings tab shows them. CN=value,O=value,C=value without spaces. The rows appeared in the tab and looked identical to the rows created in the dialog. A sample certificate for one of them still came back with Mapped email does not exist.

The reason is in SE16. The issuer hash of the rows from the dialog was one value and the issuer hash of the rows from the API was another although the issuer text was the same. The identity API hashes the string it is given and the kernel hashes the distinguished name in its internal format. The migration class converts first with method CONVERT_DN of class CL_ABAP_X509_CERTIFICATE. Our strings are in LDAP format so the conversion is from CO_FORMAT_LDAP to CO_FORMAT_INTERN.

lv_subject = cl_abap_x509_certificate=>convert_dn(
  if_dn         = 'CN=testmassload@singhvikas.com,O=POC,C=AU'
  if_format_in  = cl_abap_x509_certificate=>co_format_ldap
  if_format_out = cl_abap_x509_certificate=>co_format_intern ).

After the conversion the hashes match and the explicit mappings tab shows the subject with a space after each comma which is how the internal format looks. The issuer is the CA that signs the Cloud Connector certificates not the Cloud Connector system certificate. Both values can be read from an existing mapping in the tab.

Step 4. The ABAP class

With the first question answered the second one is easy. A custom HTTP handler in the ABAP system takes the rows and runs the same API calls that the dialog runs, and a simple BTP app reads the CSV file and calls that handler. Everything above went into one class. LOAD takes the rows and the parameters and returns a log table.

It condenses the input, removes duplicates, marks an address that appears for two users as SKIPPED, checks each user with BAPI_USER_GET_DETAIL, skips addresses that equal the SU01 address because the rule covers them, converts subject and issuer, and runs the sequence from Step 2 with EXISTS for a mapping that is already there and WOULD ADD in test mode.

READ_MAPPINGS selects USRCERTMAP.

The class also implements IF_HTTP_EXTENSION so it can be called over HTTP. GET returns the current mappings as JSON. POST reads the rows from the JSON body, calls LOAD and returns the log as JSON.

METHOD if_http_extension~handle_request.
  DATA(lv_method) = server->request->get_header_field( '~request_method' ).

  IF lv_method = 'GET'.
    respond( io_server = server
             iv_json   = /ui2/cl_json=>serialize(
               data        = VALUE ty_list( user = sy-uname mappings = read_mappings( ) )
               pretty_name = /ui2/cl_json=>pretty_mode-camel_case ) ).
    RETURN.
  ENDIF.

  DATA ls_req TYPE ty_request.
  /ui2/cl_json=>deserialize( EXPORTING json        = server->request->get_cdata( )
                                       pretty_name = /ui2/cl_json=>pretty_mode-camel_case
                             CHANGING  data        = ls_req ).
  DATA(lt_log) = load( ls_req ).
  respond( io_server = server
           iv_json   = /ui2/cl_json=>serialize(
             data        = VALUE ty_out( user = sy-uname test = ls_req-test log = lt_log )
             pretty_name = /ui2/cl_json=>pretty_mode-camel_case ) ).
ENDMETHOD.

The camel case setting of /UI2/CL_JSON maps a JSON field skipSu01 to the ABAP field SKIPSU01 without any mapping code. The user field in both answers is sy-uname. It is the proof that the call ran as the right person and the UI shows it in the header.

The class is registered in SICF under default_host/sap/bc with the class in the handler list and no logon data on the node. No logon data is the important setting. If a user were stored on the node every call would run as that user and principal propagation would be pointless. SICF service names are limited to 15 characters. The first attempt zpoc_certrule_load was cut to zpoc_certrule_l without a message. The node is zpoc_certmap.

A quick check before anything on BTP is built. Open https://host:50001/sap/bc/zpoc_certmap in a browser logged on to the ABAP system. It returns the current mappings as JSON. The Cloud Connector access control needs the same path on the mapping for the ABAP system.

Step 5. The CAP service

The CAP service has no entities. It declares one action and one function and forwards both to the ICF handler.

@path: 'loader'
@requires: 'Admin'
service LoaderService {
  action load(rows : many Row, prefix : String default 'CN=', suffix : String,
              issuer : String, skipSu01 : Boolean default true, test : Boolean default true)
    returns LoadResult;
  function mappings() returns MappingList;
}

The handler connects to the remote system declared in package.json, sends the rows in chunks of 200 and merges the logs.

this.on('load', async req => {
  const { rows = [], prefix, suffix, issuer, skipSu01, test } = req.data
  const a4h = await cds.connect.to('A4H')
  const result = { user: '', test: !!test, log: [] }
  for (let i = 0; i < rows.length; i += 200) {
    const r = await a4h.send({ method: 'POST', path: '/zpoc_certmap',
      data: { prefix, suffix, issuer, skipSu01, test, rows: rows.slice(i, i + 200) } })
    result.user = r.user || result.user
    result.log.push(...(r.log || []))
  }
  return result
})

The remote system is three lines in package.json. Kind rest, the destination name and the base path.

"A4H": { "kind": "rest", "credentials": { "destination": "A4H_PP", "path": "/sap/bc" } }

The destination does the call to the backend system. Because it is OnPremise with PrincipalPropagation the SAP Cloud SDK takes the token of the logged on user, exchanges it at the destination service and routes the call through the connectivity service to the Cloud Connector. None of that is visible in the code. The three @SAP-cloud-sdk packages connectivity, http-client and resilience in package.json are what make it work. Without them the call fails with a bare fetch failed.

Step 6. The approuter and the scope

The approuter is the standard @SAP/approuter package. It logs the user on at XSUAA, checks the scope on each route and forwards. Two routes matter.

{ "source": "^/odata/(.*)$", "destination": "srv-api", "authenticationType": "xsuaa",
  "scope": "$XSAPPNAME.Admin", "csrfProtection": false },
{ "source": "^/(.*)$", "target": "$1", "localDir": "resources/loader",
  "authenticationType": "xsuaa", "scope": "$XSAPPNAME.Admin" }

The first proxies the OData calls to the CAP service with the token forwarded. The second serves the UI page. Both need the scope Admin and the CAP service checks the same scope again with @requires. xs-security.json declares the scope, a role template and a role collection CERTRULE_Loader. After the deployment the role collection exists in the cockpit and is empty. Assigning the user is a manual step.

Step 7. The UI page

One HTML file with the UI5 controls created in JavaScript. A file uploader that reads the text file in the browser and splits it into rows, three input fields for prefix, suffix and issuer, a checkbox for skipping SU01 addresses, a table with the rows, a table with the log and a second tab with the current mappings. UI5 comes from the public CDN so there is no build step for the UI.

The input file is one line per mapping. The e-mail address and the SAP user separated by a semicolon. For us it comes from the old mapping table of the ECC system with the user and the address columns and nothing else.

newuser@singhvikas.com;DEVELOPER
newuser2@singhvikas.com;DEVELOPER
newuser3@singhvikas.com;DEVELOPER

Step 8. Build and deploy

cf login -a https://api.cf.us10-001.hana.ondemand.com
mbt build
cf deploy mta_archives/certrule-loader_1.0.0.mtar

mta.yaml declares the service module, the router module and three service instances for XSUAA, destination and connectivity. The deploy creates the services, binds them and starts the two apps. cf apps shows the router URL.

Step 9. Load from the browser

For the one step path two more addresses were created in Identity Authentication, newuser2 and newuser3. The same kind of address as newuser, in no user master, so the only thing that can map them is an explicit entry.

The file has two lines.

newuser2@singhvikas.com;DEVELOPER
newuser3@singhvikas.com;DEVELOPER

Open the router URL. The approuter redirects to the subaccount logon and from there to Identity Authentication.

The Mappings tab is the first thing to open. It shows the explicit mappings as read from USRCERTMAP through the whole chain and the header shows the ABAP user. If this tab fills nothing else can fail for a technical reason.

The Load tab. Choose the file and the two lines appear in the preview. Prefix, suffix and issuer are the values from the Cloud Connector subject pattern and CA.

Press Test run. Both lines come back as WOULD ADD and nothing is written yet. With the file from the old mapping table this is where EXISTS, RULE and SKIPPED show up and the file gets corrected before anything happens. The test run is the review of the file.

Press Load. The page asks for confirmation.

Two rows ADDED in a few seconds. When the identity framework rejects the save all rows turn into REJECTED with the first error message and nothing is written.

CERTRULE shows the three new rows together. newuser from the two manual steps at 21:38 and newuser2 and newuser3 from the app at 21:51. Same subject format, same issuer, same creator. 

Verification

The real proof is one logon with each address. newuser and newuser2 are in no user master, so the only thing that can make the call succeed is the mapping. Each address has a user in Identity Authentication with the e-mail address as login name and the status set to active, and the role collection of the small whoami app from the first post.

In a private browser window the app sends the logon to Identity Authentication. First newuser, the mapping created by hand in two steps.

The ABAP system answers DEVELOPER.

Then newuser2, the mapping written by the app from the file.

Same answer. The row written through the identity API from two strings in a file behaves exactly like the row created in the dialog from a certificate.

Summary

CERTRULE looks certificate based but what it stores is a pair of distinguished names per user. The identity framework takes those names as strings through IF_IDENTITY_CERTMAP and computes the hashes itself, so the certificate is not essential. It was only a carrier for two strings and the strings can come from a file. One ABAP class behind an HTTP handler does the load, a thin CAP service forwards to it and an approuter logs the person on. The exception list that took more than 20 hours of manual work for 500 users becomes one file and one upload that runs in a few minutes.

The real saving is in the cutover. Basis is the busiest team in that window and migrating the exception list was one more job that only they could do, entry by entry, at the point when they had the least time for it. With the loader the list is prepared ahead of time as a file, loaded in one step and checked with a test run before anything is written. The Basis team gets those hours back for the cutover work that cannot be handed to anyone else. The process becomes much more efficient and has fewer chances of error now that the manual steps are gone.

entry.title: Web Client UI API: How to retrieve the DocEntry after “Add & New” for a Sales Quotation?
entry.content:
Hi everyone,

I am developing a TypeScript UI API extension for the SAP Business One Web Client. I need to retrieve the DocEntry of a newly created Sales Quotation and use it for subsequent processing.

I have attached an after handler to the standard add button’s press event:

"on": [
    {
        "guid": "49H8VADnVmWRK4aFa5TkYy",
        "press": {
            "before": "onBeforeQuotationAdd",
            "after": "onAfterQuotationAdd"
        }
    }
]

In the controller, I read the object key as follows:

import { SDKEnv, DetailView } from "sbo/ui/core/SDKEnv";
import Event from "sbo/ui/base/Event";

public async onAfterQuotationAdd(
    oEnv: SDKEnv,
    oEvent: Event
): Promise<void> {

    const oView = await oEnv.ActiveView() as DetailView;
    const objectKey = await oView.getObjectKey();

    console.log(
        "ObjectKey:",
        JSON.stringify(objectKey, null, 2)
    );

    console.log(
        "Event parameters:",
        JSON.stringify(oEvent.getParameters(), null, 2)
    );
}

Result with “Add & View”

This works as expected. The saved quotation is displayed, and getObjectKey() returns:

{
    "object": "OQUT",
    "keys": [
        {
            "name": "DocEntry",
            "value": 347
        }
    ]
}

Result with “Add & New”

I also attached an after-press handler to the corresponding “Add & New” control.

In this case, the form has already been reset for the next quotation when the handler runs. The result contains the key name but no value:

{
    "object": "OQUT",
    "keys": [
        {
            "name": "DocEntry"
        }
    ]
}

The event parameters only contain sEventName, sViewGuid, and sCtrlGuid. They do not contain the created document’s key or the save response.

The console output also shows that onDataLoad is called before my after-press handler.

My questions

  1. Is there a supported business-object event that fires after a successful add and provides the newly created object key, independently of the subsequent navigation?

  2. Can a UI API extension access the result of the standard save operation, including the generated DocEntry?

  3. What is the recommended approach for handling this with “Add & New”, while keeping the standard save behavior?

I would like to identify the exact quotation created by this operation. Querying the highest or most recent DocEntry would not reliably identify it when multiple users are creating quotations concurrently.

Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Manuel

entry.title: Re: Removing Space between Two Blocks (PNP LDB and Custom Block) in Selection Screen
entry.content:
Hi,

The gap comes from the logical database itself, not from your block. The selection include of PNP, DBPNPSEL, ends with this statement, after the block with the selection options and the hidden parameters:

SELECTION-SCREEN SKIP 1 FOR TABLE PERNR.

The elements of the logical database always come first on selection screen 1000, so any block of the report starts one line lower.

I tested it in my S/4HANA 2023 lab with a small report with logical database PNP and one block WITH FRAME, and read the generated screen 1000. The last PNP frame (the selection block) ends on line 77, line 78 is empty, and the frame of the report starts on line 79.

From the report you can't remove that line. It is not a screen field, so LOOP AT SCREEN in AT SELECTION-SCREEN OUTPUT doesn't see it, and the selection screen versions at the end of DBPNPSEL only exclude blocks, while this SKIP is outside any block. The options I see are:

  • Live with it. Changing DBPNPSEL would be a modification of SAP code, and I wouldn't do that for one empty line.
  • Use logical database PNPCE. Its include DBPNPCESEL has no SKIP, and in the same test with PNPCE the frame of the report started right on the line after the last PNPCE frame. But PNPCE works with node PERAS (GET PERAS) and has its own selection fields, so it is only worth it if you plan to move to PNPCE anyway.

I only checked the generated screens in the 2023 lab, so please compare DBPNPSEL in your system.

entry.title: Re: SAP RAP Question: Allowing Another User to Edit Drafts
entry.content:
Hi Ajay,

Thanks for coming back with the details. The transport part I could test, so I did it in my S/4HANA 2023 lab.

I created a small managed RAP BO with draft in a package that records changes, with a request of my own, then added these two annotations to the root view entity and activated it:

@ObjectModel.lifecycle.draft.expiryBehavior: #RELATIVE_TO_PROCESSING_START
@ObjectModel.lifecycle.draft.expiryInterval: 'PT7D'

What the activation did:

  • It wrote the line in SDRAFT_LC_CONFIG: event 33 (Absolute Draft Expiry) with 2,419,200 seconds. PT7D was rejected with a warning that it is too short, the view still activated, and the line got the default of 28 days.
  • It added R3TR TABU SDRAFT_LC_CONFIG to my request, with the key "entity name + 33" in the key list. It went to the request itself, not to my task: in E071 the task had the tables, the view and the behavior definition, and the TABU entry was on the request.
  • When I deleted the view, the line disappeared from SDRAFT_LC_CONFIG again.

In the code this is CL_DRAFT_CONFIG_CDS_HANDLER, registered in the DDLS activation, calling CL_DRAFT_LIFECYCLE_CONFIG (CONFIGURATION_UPDATE and then WRITE_TRANSPORT_REQUEST). The recording is skipped for $TMP, and if it fails the activation doesn't tell you. The table is client-independent (delivery class S), which is why you see the same lines in clients 500 and 510.

So before opening the client in QA, I would check the request itself in SE09, not only the task, for R3TR TABU SDRAFT_LC_CONFIG. If it is there, it travels like any other table entry. My lab has no target system, so I couldn't test the import.

About the road map, I can't answer for SAP. One point for the CAB before dropping draft: the takeover that Manage Purchase Orders gives in 2023 is the one of an exclusive draft, and a RAP BO with draft has the same one, after the 15 minutes of the <DEFAULT> line.

entry.title: Re: ME23N needs to display the IR Reference field
entry.content:
Hi,

Before asking SAP for a new field, check what the existing Reference column in the purchase order history shows. In my S/4HANA 2023 lab it is not the reference of the invoice.

The PO history comes from EKBE, and on invoice lines EKBE-XBLNR holds the delivery note of the goods receipt the invoice refers to (field LFBNR), not the reference entered in MIRO (RBKP-XBLNR). Of the 249 invoice lines in my lab, 156 have exactly the XBLNR of their goods receipt line, and the 47 lines without a goods receipt reference all have it empty. Example: PO 4500000074 item 10, goods receipt with delivery note REFORMA-123, invoice with reference 0001. The history shows REFORMA-123 on both lines.

If you need the invoice reference next to the PO items, the released CDS views have it, so no modification is needed. This ran in my lab:

SELECT h~PurchaseOrder, h~PurchaseOrderItem, h~PurchasingHistoryDocument,
       h~PurchasingHistoryDocumentYear, h~DocumentReferenceID,
       i~SupplierInvoiceIDByInvcgParty
  FROM i_purchaseorderhistoryapi01 AS h
  INNER JOIN i_supplierinvoiceapi01 AS i
    ON  i~SupplierInvoice = h~PurchasingHistoryDocument
    AND i~FiscalYear      = h~PurchasingHistoryDocumentYear
  WHERE h~PurchaseOrder = '4500000074'
    AND h~PurchasingHistoryCategory = 'Q'
  ORDER BY h~PurchaseOrderItem, h~PurchasingHistoryDocument
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_hist).

It returned the 5 invoices of that PO. DocumentReferenceID, which is what the history shows, was REFORMA-123, empty, REFORMA-1234 twice and REFORMA-12345. SupplierInvoiceIDByInvcgParty, the invoice reference, was 0001, 0002, 0003, 0003 and 0004. Both views are released (C1) in my lab, so you can use them in ABAP Cloud as well, for example behind a small report or a custom Fiori list.

I didn't test adding a column to the history in ME23N itself.

entry.title: Re: In SAP-Query (SQ00) funktioniert nach S4-Migration di...
entry.content:
Hi,

I could reproduce the cause in my S/4HANA 2023 lab, except the part on the screen.

For a transaction as receiver, the report-report interface (function group RSTI, form TCODE_FIND_FIELDR in include LRSTIF02) takes the fields it can pass from the start screen of the transaction in TSTC: the screen fields with a parameter ID. It sets those parameter IDs and calls the transaction with AND SKIP FIRST SCREEN.

In my lab TSTC has AS03 on SAPLAIST screen 0005, "Dummy initial screen for Fiori tile". That screen has only the OK code field. Its PBO calls form DISPATCHING_TCODE, which reads the parameter IDs AN1, AN2 and BUK and then opens the new Fiori asset master data UI, if that is active, or does LEAVE TO SCREEN 100, the classic initial screen with ANLA-ANLN1 (AN1), ANLA-ANLN2 (AN2) and ANLA-BUKRS (BUK). In my lab the new asset master data is not active, so it goes to screen 100.

I ran the interface's own form TCODE_FIND_FIELDR for these start screens:

  • AS03, SAPLAIST 0005: no field
  • SAPLAIST 0100: ANLA-ANLN1 = AN1, ANLA-ANLN2 = AN2, ANLA-BUKRS = BUK, RA02S-SICHT = AVW
  • AW01N, program AW01N screen 0005: no field, so the Asset Explorer is not a way around it

So the interface finds nothing to pass for AS03, no parameter ID is set, and screen 100 comes up empty. SAPLAIST also has no form RSTI_SELECTION_EXIT, the hook where a receiver can declare its fields to the interface (I searched the 897 includes of SAPLAIST that I could read).

What worked in the lab is a small report as receiver, because for a report the interface takes the fields from its selection screen. This is the report I tested, only the name is different:

REPORT zas03_from_query.
PARAMETERS: p_bukrs TYPE anla-bukrs,
            p_anln1 TYPE anla-anln1,
            p_anln2 TYPE anla-anln2.

START-OF-SELECTION.
  SET PARAMETER ID 'BUK' FIELD p_bukrs.
  SET PARAMETER ID 'AN1' FIELD p_anln1.
  SET PARAMETER ID 'AN2' FIELD p_anln2.
  CALL TRANSACTION 'AS03' WITH AUTHORITY-CHECK AND SKIP FIRST SCREEN.

With a line like yours (ANLA-BUKRS 1410, ANLA-ANLN1 000010000000, ANLA-ANLN2 0000), the interface's forms REPORT_FIND_FIELDR, FIELD_TRANSF and REPORT_FIND_PARAMS mapped the three values to P_BUKRS, P_ANLN1 and P_ANLN2 by data element, ready for the SUBMIT. In the query you assign it in the report assignment as an ABAP report, instead of AS03.

What I could not test is the dialog: the double-click and AS03 on the screen. The report sets AN1, AN2 and BUK, DISPATCHING_TCODE reads them and screen 100 has GET PARAMETER on the three fields, so the values should arrive. Please check whether AS03 opens the asset directly or stops on the initial screen with the values filled.

Sorry for answering in English.

entry.title: Re: Sales order issue in customer display
entry.content:
Hi,

The description next to the sold-to party in the sales order is not KNA1-NAME1. It is the short form of the address. In my S/4HANA 2023 lab the order builds it in form KUAGV-TXTPA_ERMITTELN (include MV45AF0K_KUAGV-TXTPA_ERMITTELN), which calls function module SD_ADDRESS_BUILD. For an address from the master data, SD_ADDRESS_BUILD calls CL_ADDRESS_FORMAT, method FORMATTED_NAME_AND_POSTAL_ADDR, so the text follows the address formatting, and that can include the title.

I called SD_ADDRESS_BUILD in the lab for customers with different titles in the address:

  • Title 0003 "Company": "Domestic BR Customer 1, (street), São Paulo - SP, (postal code)". No title.
  • Title 0002 "Mr.": "Sr. (name), (city), (postal code), Brasil". The title comes first, in the logon language (I was logged on in Portuguese).
  • No title: name and address only.

The difference is in table TSAD3: 0003 is a title for organizations, 0001 and 0002 (Ms. and Mr.) are titles for persons. In my test only the person title went into the short form. KNA1-NAME1 had no title in any case, and KNA1-ANRED has the title text.

So I would check which title the business partner has in its address. If customer 50000580 is a company with a person title like Mr. or Ms., an organization title (or none) should take it out of the order screen. One more case from the same code: if the address was changed in the order itself, the text is built from that document address instead.

What I didn't test: changing the title of an existing customer and looking at the order again, and your output forms, which can use other address functions.

entry.title: Agentic AI on BTP: Calling an Agent from Your UI5 App
entry.content:
Introduction

What if your UI5 app could hand a receipt to an agent and get back the id of the draft expense it created? Not through a chat window, but behind a simple button in the app your users already work with.

This is the sixth post in the series. The previous one connected agents to SAP OData services without an MCP server: https://community.sap.com/t5/technology-blog-posts-by-members/agentic-ai-on-btp-connecting-agents-to-sap-odata-apis-without-an-mcp-server/ba-p/14506364

In this blog post, I’ll show you how a UI5 app calls an agent from my multi-agent app on BTP through two API calls and what you need to configure for it.

Problem

Adding an agent to an existing UI5 app usually means building a new CAP app that holds the agent. For every use case:

  • A new app to build and run. Code, deploy, secure and maintain it next to the UI5 app.
  • Everything again. Model access, destinations, the user’s identity to SAP and the tools the agent needs.
  • The agent lives in code. Changing its instructions or tools means a new deployment.
  • A chat is not what a form needs. The app wants a structured answer it can use, not a paragraph of text.

All of that already exists in my agent app: agents configured in the admin UI, connectors, OData services and identity per service. What was missing was a way for another app to call one of those agents.

Solution

The app now has an invoke API. A UI5 app calls one agent by its slug, as the signed-in user, with a text and optional files. It gets back a structured result plus a list of what the agent changed in SAP. Two calls:

  • POST /api/invoke/{slug}: starts the run, multipart with input (text) and files (PNG, JPEG or PDF)
  • GET /api/invoke/runs/{run_id}: the status and the outcome

No new CAP app. The agent stays in the agent app, the UI5 app only needs a destination and a few lines of JavaScript. 🙂

Step 1: Expose the agent

On the agent in the admin UI, give it an API slug and switch on “Expose to the invoke API”. Next to that you define the result the agent has to hand back as a JSON schema:

{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "expense_id": { "type": "string" },
    "status": { "type": "string", "enum": ["draft"] }
  },
  "required": ["expense_id", "status"],
  "additionalProperties": false
}

The agent gets a submit_result tool for that run. What it hands in is checked against the schema, a wrong object goes back to the model to correct. A run that ends with only text fails with no_result, so your app never reads a result the model only talked about.

The attachments are limited per agent: which file types, the size (default 10 MB), the number of files (default 5) and the PDF pages (default 20).

Step 2: Give the users the role collection

The API is behind its own scope invoke. Assign the role collection Agent Invoker to the users of the UI5 app. The run is theirs: the agent calls SAP with their identity, through the OData services that run as the signed-in user.

Step 3: Destination and route

The UI5 app reaches the agent app through a destination that exchanges the user’s token for one of the agent app’s XSUAA. In the same subaccount, this can be done with OAuth2UserTokenExchange:

Name=agent-invoke
Type=HTTP
URL=https://<agent-backend-host>
ProxyType=Internet
Authentication=OAuth2UserTokenExchange
clientId=<clientid of the agent app's xsuaa>
clientSecret=<clientsecret of the agent app's xsuaa>
tokenServiceURL=https://<subdomain>.authentication.<region>.hana.ondemand.com/oauth/token

(For an app in another subaccount, use OAuth2SAMLBearerAssertion with a trust between both subaccounts.)

In the xs-app.json of the UI5 app, one route maps everything under agent/ to the invoke API:

{
  "source": "^/agent/(.*)$",
  "target": "/api/invoke/$1",
  "destination": "agent-invoke",
  "authenticationType": "xsuaa",
  "csrfProtection": true
}

Step 4: Call the agent

For the upload I use a FileUploader and keep the selected files in the controller:

<u:FileUploader id="receipt" change=".onFileChange" fileType="png,jpg,jpeg,pdf" />
<Button text="Create expense from receipt" press=".onCreateFromReceipt" />

The call itself is a fetch with FormData (MessageBox comes from sap/m/MessageBox). Don’t set the Content-Type yourself, the browser adds the multipart boundary. The URL is resolved through the manifest, so it also works when the app runs in a Work Zone site:

onFileChange: function (oEvent) {
    this._files = Array.from(oEvent.getParameter("files") || []);
},

onCreateFromReceipt: async function () {
    const sBase = this.getOwnerComponent().getManifestObject().resolveUri("agent/");
    const oForm = new FormData();
    oForm.append("input", "Create a draft expense from this receipt.");
    (this._files || []).forEach((oFile) => oForm.append("files", oFile, oFile.name));

    this.getView().setBusy(true);
    try {
        const oRun = await this._invoke(sBase, "expense-expert", oForm);
        this._handleRun(oRun);
    } catch (oError) {
        MessageBox.error(oError.message);
    } finally {
        this.getView().setBusy(false);
    }
},

_invoke: async function (sBase, sSlug, oForm) {
    const sToken = await this._csrfToken(sBase);
    // wait up to 20 seconds, a quick run answers right away
    const oRes = await fetch(sBase + encodeURIComponent(sSlug) + "?wait=20", {
        method: "POST",
        headers: { "X-CSRF-Token": sToken },
        body: oForm
    });
    const oBody = await oRes.json().catch(() => ({}));
    if (oRes.status === 200) { return oBody; }                 // finished in time
    if (oRes.status === 202) { return this._poll(sBase, oBody.run_id); }
    if (oRes.status === 409 && oBody.run_id) {                  // already running for this user
        return this._poll(sBase, oBody.run_id);
    }
    throw new Error(oBody.detail || "The agent could not be started");
},

_poll: async function (sBase, sRunId) {
    for (;;) {
        await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 3000));
        const oRun = await (await fetch(sBase + "runs/" + encodeURIComponent(sRunId))).json();
        if (oRun.status !== "running") { return oRun; }
    }
},

_csrfToken: async function (sBase) {
    const oRes = await fetch(sBase, { method: "HEAD", headers: { "X-CSRF-Token": "Fetch" } });
    return oRes.headers.get("X-CSRF-Token");
}

Step 5: Use the result

This is what comes back when the run is done:

{
  "status": "completed",
  "result": { "expense_id": "4711", "status": "draft" },
  "writes": [
    { "service": "expenses", "entity_set": "ExpenseReports", "operation": "create",
      "key": { "ExpenseId": "4711" }, "outcome": "ok" }
  ],
  "text": null,
  "activity": [ ... ],
  "error": null
}

result follows your schema. writes comes from the audit log of the OData services, so the key in there is the one SAP returned, not one the model made up. activity holds every tool call of the run, you can even show it while polling.

Next, the app refreshes and opens the new draft:

_handleRun: function (oRun) {
    if (oRun.status !== "completed") {
        MessageBox.error("The agent could not finish: " + (oRun.error || oRun.status));
        return;
    }
    this.getView().getModel().refresh();
    this.getOwnerComponent().getRouter().navTo("expense", { id: oRun.result.expense_id });
}

Good to know

  • One run per user per agent. A second call while one is running answers 409 with the running run_id, at most 8 runs per app instance (429).
  • Five minutes. A run that takes longer ends with timeout.
  • Files stay in memory. Attachments are only kept for the run, never stored or logged. The file type is checked on its content, not on its name.
  • A failed run keeps its result. If something fails after the agent handed in its result, you still get it with the error code.

Conclusion

Adding an agent to a UI5 app doesn’t need a new CAP app anymore. The agent is configured once in the agent app with its tools, its OData services and its identity. Any UI5 app can then call it with two API calls.

The structured result is what makes it usable in a form: the app gets an object it can rely on and a list of what was changed in SAP, instead of a chat answer it has to interpret.

Contributions and feedback are welcome, the full source code is on GitHub: https://github.com/lemaiwo/btp-dynamic-multiagent-app

entry.title: Re: Unable to Retrieve Trading Partner No. and Group Acco...
entry.content:
Hi,

Both fields are in I_GLAccountInChartOfAccounts. In my S/4HANA 2023 lab the DDL source of the view maps them like this:

  • Group Account Number = CorporateGroupAccount = SKA1-BILKT
  • Trading Partner No. = PartnerCompany = SKA1-VBUND (data element RASSC, "Company ID of Trading Partner")

SKA1 has no RASSC or ALTKT field. RASSC is only the data element of VBUND, and ALTKT is SKB1-ALTKT, the alternative account number in the company code, which is not the group account.

About the accounts you don't find: the view selects from SKA1 with no WHERE condition, so every account of every chart of accounts is in it. In my lab, with my user, the view returns the same 20,409 rows as SKA1, and joining the ledger 0L line items with the view kept all 4,335 lines. These are the three things I would check. The first two I could reproduce:

  • Join on both keys, ChartOfAccounts and GLAccount, with the chart of accounts of the line item. The view has one row per chart of accounts and account. In my lab account 0021120000 exists in two charts (YCOA and PCJW), and the line items only use YCOA.
  • Use the internal format of the account number. GLAccount = '21120000' returned nothing, GLAccount = '0021120000' returned the account.
  • Authorization. The view has access control (AccessControl.authorizationCheck with value CHECK), so a user without authorization for the account master data can get fewer rows. I didn't test this with a restricted user.

One more trap: PartnerCompany in I_GLAccountLineItem is the trading partner of the posting, not the one in the account master. In my lab it is filled on the same 52 lines where ACDOCA-RASSC is filled. Account 1110201001 has trading partner 001991 in the master data, and its line items have PartnerCompany empty.

This ran in my lab. I_GLAccountLineItem, I_GLAccountInChartOfAccounts and I_GLAccountText are all released for ABAP Cloud (C1) in 2023:

SELECT l~CompanyCode, l~AccountingDocument, l~LedgerGLLineItem, l~GLAccount,
       a~CorporateGroupAccount,
       a~PartnerCompany AS AccountTradingPartner,
       a~\_CorporateGroupAccount\_Text[ (1) LEFT OUTER WHERE Language = 'E' ]-GLAccountName AS GroupAccountName
  FROM I_GLAccountLineItem AS l
  INNER JOIN I_GLAccountInChartOfAccounts AS a
    ON  a~ChartOfAccounts = l~ChartOfAccounts
    AND a~GLAccount       = l~GLAccount
  WHERE l~Ledger = '0L'
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_items).

It returned the 4,335 lines, 3,214 of them with a group account. Two examples: account 0021120000 (chart YCOA) has group account 0000211100 "Trade payables" in the group chart YGR1, and account 1110201001 has group account 0000121800 "Other receivables" and trading partner 001991. The group account name comes through the view's own association _CorporateGroupAccount and its _Text, so you don't need a second join for it.

What I didn't test: a user with restricted authorizations, and S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. I only checked that the views are released in my 2023 system.

entry.title: Re: Negative sign is needed in front of the amount fields...
entry.content:
Hi,

Before you change it, look at how INVOIC02 already carries the sign. I read IDOC_OUTPUT_INVOIC (function group VEDF) in my S/4HANA 2023 lab:

  • E1EDK01-BSART is CRME or INVO (FORM FILL_E1EDK01). CL_SD_DOC_CATEGORY_UTIL=>IS_ANY_RETOUR decides it, and in my lab it returns true for categories O (credit memo), N (invoice cancellation) and 6 (intercompany credit memo). A credit memo list also gets CRME.
  • The totals in E1EDS01 come from the billing document values (VBDKR-NETWR and the tax sum), and those are positive for these documents too. The 10 invoice cancellations in my lab all have a positive NETWR.
  • In the condition segments E1EDK05 and E1EDP05 the sign is removed on purpose: if KWERT is negative, BETRG gets -1 * KWERT and ALCKZ gets '-' (FORM FILL_E1EDK05, the same for E1EDP05).

So a receiver that follows the standard takes the sign from BSART and ALCKZ. That is the main impact: if you also put a minus in the amounts, a partner whose mapping already uses BSART or ALCKZ will reverse it twice. And if a negative value does reach an amount field, the standard formatting (FORM MOVE_FIELD moves the number into the character field and then does CONDENSE) puts the minus at the end. I ran that in my lab: -1234.56 into E1EDS01-SUMME gives 1234.56-. My lab even has an invoice with NETWR -7000.00, which would go out as 7000.00- with BSART INVO.

If your partners need the minus in front, the place is EXIT_SAPLVEDF_002 (enhancement LVEDF001), as the other answer says, or the BAdI SD_INVOICE_IDOC_OUTPUT_INT (spot SD_INVOICE_IDOC_OUTPUT), method IDOC_DATA_APPEND. Both are called from FORM CUSTOMER_FUNCTION (include LVEDFF0C) right after each segment is appended, so the new segment is the last line of INT_EDIDD. This is the logic I tested in my lab, on an INT_EDIDD with an E1EDK01 line and an E1EDS01 line filled the way the standard fills them:

DATA: ls_edidd TYPE edidd,
      ls_k01   TYPE e1edk01,
      ls_seg   TYPE e1eds01.
DATA(lv_idx) = lines( int_edidd[] ).
READ TABLE int_edidd[] INTO ls_edidd INDEX lv_idx.
IF ls_edidd-segnam = 'E1EDS01'.
  READ TABLE int_edidd[] INTO DATA(ls_head) WITH KEY segnam = 'E1EDK01'.
  ls_k01 = ls_head-sdata.
  ls_seg = ls_edidd-sdata.
  IF ls_k01-bsart = 'CRME' AND ls_seg-sumid <> '001' AND ls_seg-summe IS NOT INITIAL.
    ls_seg-summe = |-{ ls_seg-summe }|.
    ls_edidd-sdata = ls_seg.
    MODIFY int_edidd[] FROM ls_edidd INDEX lv_idx.
  ENDIF.
ENDIF.

With BSART CRME the total 1234.56 became -1234.56, with INVO it stayed 1234.56. SUMID 001 is the number of items, so it is left out. The same pattern works for E1EDP26-BETRG; in E1EDK05 and E1EDP05 the sign is already in ALCKZ. With many countries I would switch it on per partner (CONTROL_RECORD_OUT-RCVPRN is available in the exit), not for everyone.

What I didn't test: a real INVOIC IDoc. My lab has no INVOIC output set up, so I ran the standard formatting and the exit logic on their own, not inside the output run.

entry.title: Re: Need help deciding on the best field for range partit...
entry.content:
Hi, 

For a 1.2B-row table with both a contract identifier and a date field, multilevel partitioning (HASH + RANGE) is the recommended 

Example: Hash on CONTRACT_INT (for load distribution) 
         + Range on date field (for data lifecycle & pruning)
ALTER TABLE YOUR_TABLE 
PARTITION BY HASH (CONTRACT_INT) PARTITIONS 4,
             RANGE (DATE_COLUMN)
(
  PARTITION '20200101' <= VALUES < '20210101',
  PARTITION '20210101' <= VALUES < '20220101',
  PARTITION '20220101' <= VALUES < '20230101',
  PARTITION '20230101' <= VALUES < '20240101',
  PARTITION OTHERS
);

Benefits of this approach:

  • HASH level distributes data evenly across nodes (important for scale-out).
  • RANGE level on the date column enables partition pruning for time-based queries and efficient delta merges (old partitions stop accumulating deltas).
  • The PARTITION OTHERS catches future dates — but note: if you use ADD PARTITION frequently, avoid an OTHERS partition, as splitting it is a costly exclusive-lock operation.

1. Range Partitioning
https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_HANA_PLATFORM/6b94445c94ae495c83a19646e7c3fd56/c338627bbb571014ae7d9533861b600f.html?locale=en-US&state=PRODUCTION&version=2.0.08&q=range%20partition

2. Hash-Range Partitioning
https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_HANA_PLATFORM/6b94445c94ae495c83a19646e7c3fd56/c316a83bbb571014a56dc82fbcfa4cc3.html?locale=en-US&state=PRODUCTION&version=2.0.08&q=range%20partition

entry.title: Re: DMS
entry.content:
Hi,

What you see is the template copy. Version 01 is created with version 00 as the template, and the originals of the template are copied into the new version. In my S/4HANA 2023 lab both CV110_DOC_CREATE_WITH_TEMPLATE (dialog) and CVAPI_DOC_CREATE_WITH_TEMPLATE (API) call CV120_DOC_FILES_COPY for this. This is what it does:

  • An original that is checked in is not copied as a new file. The new version gets a reference to the same original (LO_IS_REF = 'X'), and it is not offered in the selection popup. That is why version 01 shows the file of version 00.
  • An original that is not checked in is copied as a new original, and in dialog a popup lets you choose which originals to take.
  • Before both cases the function module checks two switches that skip the copy completely: TDWA-NEW_VERS_IGNORE ("Ignore originals") for the document type, and the parameter COPYORIGINALS = space.

I called CV120_DOC_FILES_COPY in my lab for a new version 04 with version 03 as the template, document type with KPro, in batch mode (no popup, nothing saved). 1 original went into the new version. With NEW_VERS_IGNORE = 'X' (set only in the buffer of the function group, not in the table) it was 0, back to space it was 1 again. With COPYORIGINALS = space it was 0.

The catch with NEW_VERS_IGNORE: in my 2023 lab the field is in the maintenance view V_TDWA_1 (as NEW_VERS_SIGNORE) but on none of the DC10 screens, so I found no standard way to set it, and I would not change the table directly. If your release shows "Ignore originals" in the document type details, that is the answer without code.

For the dialog I would use the classic BAdI DOCUMENT_MAIN01, method AFTER_READ_DATA. CV110_DOC_CREATE_WITH_TEMPLATE calls it (through CV115_EXIT_AFTER_READ_DATA) right after the copy and before the screen, with the new DRAW and the copied originals in DOCFILES, a changing parameter that replaces the list. Two details from the code:

  • TCODE in this call is 'CV01' (constant C_DMS_CREATE), not 'CV01N', so a check on 'CV01N' never matches.
  • DRAW-DOKVR_VL (the template version) is filled here, but it is also saved with the document: my versions created from a template keep it in DRAW. So check TCODE as well, not only DOKVR_VL.
METHOD if_ex_document_main01~after_read_data.
  " version created from a template: DOCFILES has the copied originals
  IF tcode = 'CV01' AND draw-dokar = 'DRW' AND draw-dokvr_vl IS NOT INITIAL.
    CLEAR docfiles.
  ENDIF.
ENDMETHOD.

Put your document type instead of DRW. The same BAdI also runs when a version is created by BAPI (CVAPI_DOC_CREATE_WITH_TEMPLATE calls it with API_FLAG = 'X'). For programs you don't need it: BAPI_DOCUMENT_CREATENEWVRS2 has COPYORIGINALS (default 'X') and passes it down to CV120_DOC_FILES_COPY, and BAPI_DOCUMENT_CREATENEWVERSION hands it to VRS2 when you pass no file. That is the 0 above.

What I didn't test: saving a real version in CV01N or CV02N, an implementation of the BAdI, and a checked-in original. The original of my template was not checked in, so my run went through the copy, not the reference. That the two switches come before both cases I only saw in the code.

entry.title: Re: Completed/Archived Goals still showing in Performance...
entry.content:
We were facing a similar challenge with an evergreen Development Goal Plan where the Development Goal Plan itself has an end date of 31/12/9999. Although our Performance Review templates have their own cycle-specific start and end dates, those dates are not providing the expected boundary for the Development Goal content pulled into the form.

As a result, completed development goals from previous years continued to appear on newly launched Performance Review forms, including goals that had been closed several years earlier.

Creating a new Development Goal Plan for every performance cycle was something we wanted to avoid, as the intention is to retain a single evergreen plan and preserve the employee's development-goal history.

Our proposed solution is therefore:

  • Retain the existing Development Goal Plan as an evergreen plan.
  • Introduce an Archived goal category and corresponding Archived status.
  • Configure the completion trigger so that an archived goal is moved into the Archived category.
  • In the Performance Review form XML, configure the Development Goals section with an obj-category filter so that only goals belonging to the active Development Goals category are pulled into the form.
  • Archived goals consequently remain part of the employee's evergreen Development Goal Plan but are excluded from newly launched Performance Review forms.

This gives us the behaviour we were looking for: employees can maintain development goals over time in a single evergreen plan, while historical/archived goals don't continue to follow them into every subsequent Performance Review cycle.

We've successfully validated the configuration in our testing. I'm interested to hear from others who have implemented a similar evergreen Development Goal Plan design.

Are there any known gotchas, downstream impacts or considerations with using the goal category and obj-category filtering in this way, particularly with TIH, LMS, SCDP modules and over multiple Performance Management cycles.

entry.title: Clarification on POI-Based Replication vs. BDC Delta Sharing for Persistent Databricks Ingestion
entry.content:
We would like SAP to clarify the fundamental differences, intended use cases, and commercial positioning of POI-based Replication Flow and BDC Connect / Delta Sharing.

Our business objective is to persist SAP data within Databricks, where we will maintain our Bronze, Silver, and Gold layers for enterprise analytics and reporting.

With this objective in mind, we would appreciate SAP's clarification on the following questions:

entry.title: Re: Distribution channel and conditions type not availabl...
entry.content:
Hi,

There are two different causes here. The distribution channel is not in the standard XML at all, and which condition lines get into it depends on the print ID in the pricing procedure. I checked both in my S/4HANA 2023 lab, with the data provider behind the billing form templates SDBIL_CI_STANDARD_* in output management (FDP_V3_BD_STANDARD).

Distribution channel

  • No entity of FDP_V3_BD_STANDARD has a distribution channel. I searched its model class, and the same search finds ConditionType in the pricing nodes. The header is filled from the billing document buffer, and VTWEG is in that buffer but is not mapped to the header.
  • The header takes the custom fields of business context SD_BILLINGDOC (billing document header), and right after that the FDP calls BAdI SD_BIL_PRINT_STANDARD_HEAD (spot ES_SD_BIL_EXTEND), method MODIFY_OUTPUT. The BAdI gets the whole header as I_BillingDocumentBasic and can change the custom fields in BILLINGDOC_EXTENSION_OUT.
  • I_BillingDocumentBasic has DistributionChannel. For my test invoice it returns 10.

So the way is a custom field in business context Billing Document, enabled for the billing document form, and an implementation of SD_BIL_PRINT_STANDARD_HEAD with one line (YY1_DISTCHANNEL stands for the name of your field):

billingdoc_extension_out-yy1_distchannel = billingdoc-distributionchannel.

No SELECT is needed, because the FDP already reads the billing document for the BAdI. Then the field is in the XML and you can place it in the form.

ZMAR, ZLOG and the metal cost subtotal

The price lines in the XML are not read from the document directly. CL_FDP_V3_BD_FORM_UTILITY, method GET_PRICE_CONDITIONS_ITEM_NEW, calls RV_PRICE_PRINT_REFRESH and RV_PRICE_PRINT_ITEM, and only what RV_PRICE_PRINT_ITEM returns becomes ItemPricingCondition. That function keeps only the steps that have a print ID in the pricing procedure (V/08, field T683S-DRUKZ).

I called it in my lab the same way the FDP does, for an invoice item with 128 condition records. Its procedure has a print ID in only 3 of 234 steps: X in steps 300 and 750, A (totals) in step 600.

  • As it is: 2 lines, step 300 (a price condition) and step 750 (a subtotal). VPRS, statistical with 2.50, was not there.
  • Print ID X for VPRS (changed only in the procedure buffer of the function group, in memory, not in the table): 3 lines, VPRS 2.50 came in.
  • Print ID "a" for VPRS: 2 lines again, no VPRS.

The last one is a trap. If any step of the item has the old value X, the function uses the old logic and prints only X. The newer values a, b, c, d (item) and A to D (totals) only count when no step has X. So give ZMAR, ZLOG and the subtotal the same kind of print ID the rest of your procedure uses.

Three more things I saw in the code but did not test:

  • Accrual conditions (KRUEK) are never printed in SD. If ZLOG is an accrual, the print ID will not bring it.
  • With the old logic a line needs a value other than zero (tax lines are the exception), and a subtotal without condition type is printed only if its value is different from the line before it.
  • The print ID is read from the procedure at print time. The document conditions (PRCD_ELEMENTS) have no print field, and in my test the result for an existing invoice changed with the buffer. So existing invoices get the change too, and so does every output that prints price conditions with that procedure, not only your form. If ZMAR must not show on other forms, filter it in your form, or fill an item custom field in BAdI SD_BIL_PRINT_STANDARD_ITEM instead.

What I didn't test: a custom field, an implementation of the two BAdIs, and a real output with the form. I didn't change the print ID in V/08, only in memory for the test.

entry.title: Re: Hungarian Company VAT Number Billing Document Output
entry.content:
Hi,

There is no standard field for the domestic number in the billing document output, so yes, it needs the BAdI. The only company tax number that reaches the XML is the VAT registration number. I checked where it comes from in my S/4HANA 2023 lab, in the data provider of the form templates SDBIL_CI_STANDARD_* (FDP_V3_BD_STANDARD) and in the Hungarian country version.

Where the company number comes from

  • It is CompanyVATRegistration in the TaxationTerms node. CL_FDP_V3_BD_FORM_UTILITY, method GET_TAXATION_TERMS, fills it with the company code and the tax departure country of the invoice header.
  • I called that method for the Hungarian country template company code of my lab (HU01). With departure country HU it returned HU12345678, the same value as the VAT registration number in the company code data (T001-STCEG). With departure country DE it came back empty, because HU01 has no VAT registration for DE in T001N. So what you get there is the VAT registration number for the departure country, from T001 or T001N.
  • The structure behind that node also has COMPANY_CODE_TIN and TAX_NUMBER0 to TAX_NUMBER5, from a localization append. The method doesn't fill them (empty in my call), and they are not in the model of either data provider, so they never get to the XML.
  • The Hungarian version doesn't add it. In my lab, package GLO_LOG_HU has the form template SDBIL_CI_STANDARD_HU and the data provider FDP_V3_BD_STANDARD_GLO_HU. Its data provider class redefines only the header: it calls the standard header method and then adds the accounting document number. Its model has no tax number property.
  • Even the eDocument for the Hungarian online invoice (CL_EDOC_MAP_HU_INV, method FILL_COMPANY_CODE_ID) takes only the 8 digit taxpayer ID, from the VAT registration number (T001-STCEG or T001N), or the group number (T007F-UMSNR) when the company code is in a VAT group (T001-UMKRS).

The BAdI

The standard header method calls BAdI SD_BIL_PRINT_STANDARD_HEAD (spot ES_SD_BIL_EXTEND), method MODIFY_OUTPUT, when the header is filled, and the Hungarian data provider calls that standard method first. So the same way works for SDBIL_CI_STANDARD_HU: a custom field in business context Billing Document, enabled for the billing document form, and MODIFY_OUTPUT fills it in BILLINGDOC_EXTENSION_OUT with the domestic number of the invoice company code (BILLINGDOC-COMPANYCODE). Then you place the field in your copy of the form.

Where you read the number from in the BAdI depends on where you keep it. That part I could not try, because my lab has no statutory reporting parameters for Hungary.

What I didn't test: the custom field, an implementation of the BAdI, a real output with SDBIL_CI_STANDARD_HU, and reading the number from the statutory reporting configuration. The eDocument part I only read in the code. I had no invoice for HU01, so I called the method with the header values such an invoice passes (company code HU01, departure country HU, then DE).

entry.title: Re: To add custom logic to exclude specific document type...
entry.content:
Hi,

KALC_ES_CYCLE_CHECK won't do it. It's the check of the cycle definition, not a hook in the run, and I found nothing in the run that filters sender values by document type. I checked it in my S/4HANA 2023 lab.

What KALC_ES_CYCLE_CHECK is

  • The spot has one BAdI, KALC_CYCLE_CHECK (interface IF_KALC_BADI_CYCLE_CHECK, filters KIND_OF_CHECK and TEMPLATE). Its only method, START_CHECK, receives the cycle key (structure KALC_CYCLE_KEY: TAB, CYCLE, SDATE) and an optional template, and gives back check results (KALC_CYCLECHECK_RESULTS). It never gets the sender values, so it can add messages to the check, but it can't change what the cycle reads.
  • SAP delivers 19 implementations of it in KALC_CYCLE_CHECK_IMPL, one class per check.

What else there is

  • KSU5 runs program SAPMKGA2. The only SAP enhancements I found for allocations are authorization checks: SAPMKGA2, "Allocation: Execute Authorization Check for Cycle" (EXIT_SAPMKGA2_001), and SAPLKAL1 and SAPMKAL1 for cycle maintenance. They decide who may run or change a cycle, not which values it takes.
  • The other two BAdIs I found, KALC_NGA_AUTHORITY_CHECK and KALC_NGA_TAGS, belong to the allocation log.
  • The allocation on the universal journal also calls the classic BAdI FAGL_ALLO_SUBSTITUTE ("Substitution in the Allocation"), for field values of the allocation lines. It's not a sender filter.

Why document type is not available in the segment

  • The fields you can use to restrict senders come from the allocation control table T811I. For an actual assessment on the classic cycle table CCSS (KSU5) they are cost center, cost element, cost object, business process, functional area, fund, grant and recovery indicator. CCSS doesn't even have a document type field.
  • S/4HANA also has a cost center allocation on the universal journal (cycle table ACDOC_CC; in my system the CC Alloc transactions like FINS_ALLOC_CC_A5 run the same program SAPMKGA2). It reads ACDOCA, and its data structure ACDOC_ALLOC does have BLART. But T811I lists only account, cost center, functional area, fund, grant, budget period and recovery indicator as sender fields there. So that version doesn't give you document type either.

What I would do

Make the exclusion through a field the segment does have. If the documents you want to leave out are posted to their own cost elements, take those out of the sender cost element group. If they share cost elements with the postings you want to keep, the split has to exist in the data before the cycle runs: those documents have to land on a cost element or a cost center that the segment leaves out.

What I didn't test: I didn't run KSU5 or the CC Alloc transactions, and I didn't implement the BAdI or the exit. I didn't check the Manage Allocations app or an ECC system. The field lists above are what the control table says for an actual assessment in my system.

entry.title: From Fast MRP to Flexible Planning: The Functional Evolution of MRP Live from S/4HANA 1511 to 2025
entry.content:
Introduction

When SAP introduced MRP Live with SAP S/4HANA 1511 in 2015, the headline was speed. Traditional MRP moved large volumes of planning data between the database and the application layer. MRP Live was redesigned for SAP HANA so that significantly more planning work could be performed close to the data.

For planners, however, the more important story is not only performance. The real evolution has been the gradual expansion from a fast but restricted planning engine into the normal MRP engine for a broad range of S/4HANA supply-chain scenarios.

That journey was not completed in one release. Early implementations often required a mixture of MRP Live and classical MRP. Over subsequent releases, SAP expanded functional coverage, improved MRP-area-based planning, introduced better planner applications and corrected release-specific planning behaviors.

MRP Live in Business Language

MRP answers three familiar questions:

  1. What do we need?
  2. When do we need it?
  3. Should we make it, buy it or transfer it from another location?

Suppose several distribution centers forecast demand for the same finished product. Planning must:

  • Compare demand with stock and scheduled receipts at each DC.
  • Generate stock-transfer requirements toward the supplying plant.
  • Create a planned order at the manufacturing plant.
  • Explode the bill of material.
  • Generate planned orders for manufactured components and purchase requisitions for externally procured components.

MRP Live does not change this business objective. It changes how efficiently the system processes the planning network. SAP training material describes MRP Live as parallel planning of multiple materials using SAP HANA, while classical MRP is more commonly associated with sequential or overnight batch processing.

The following illustration shows both the release journey and the practical mixed-planning principle.

 Figure 1: MRP Live evolved from a performance-led innovation into the normal planning engine for broad S/4HANA scenarios, while mixed-mode processing and classical MRP remain practical safeguards for exceptions.

The Evolution by Release

A warning is important before building a timeline: SAP did not publish one clean, cumulative list showing every restriction removed in every release. Some changes appear in release documentation, some in simplification items and others only in SAP Notes. The chronology below therefore highlights verifiable functional milestones rather than inventing an enhancement for every annual release.

Release

Functional milestone

Why it mattered

1511

MRP Live introduced as the HANA-optimized planning run. SAP also standardized planning around the plant and MRP-area levels rather than the old separate storage-location MRP model.

Established the new planning architecture, but with narrower functional coverage than classical MRP.

1610–1709

Early functional expansion and correction phase. More normal planning scenarios could be executed through MD01N, while unsupported combinations continued to be handled through classical processing.

Organizations could begin using MRP Live for larger material populations while retaining a hybrid model.

1709–1809

Selection, performance and special-scenario handling continued to mature. SAP Note history includes 2690899 – MRP Live: Selection with MRP Controller, applicable to early S4CORE releases, and corrections for materials not selected by the MRP cockpit.

Helped organizations control planning scope and troubleshoot why materials were not planned.

1909 FPS01

SAP introduced MRP-area profiles that could provide default behavior when storage-location MRP areas were assigned—for example, excluding a location from planning or defaulting special procurement settings.

Reduced repetitive master-data maintenance and made storage-location-level planning through MRP areas more manageable.

2020

MRP-area profiles became part of the documented MRP configuration model; the broader Fiori planning and responsibility framework also continued to grow.

The evolution was increasingly about operational usability, not merely the core calculation engine.

2021

SAP added applications such as Schedule Unassigning of MRP Areas and documented time-dependent safety-stock functionality in the MRP portfolio.

Improved mass maintenance and enabled more flexible planning buffers over time.

2022–2023

Functional scope was comparatively mature, with development increasingly focused on corrections, special planning combinations, planner applications and performance. SAP Note 3041082, for example, corrected net-change planning behavior for MPN-MRP sets across S4CORE 102–106.

Demonstrated that a scenario might be conceptually supported but still require a release-specific correction.

2025

No single major “MRP Live 2.0” engine milestone was identified. The practical picture is a mature MRP Live engine surrounded by ongoing corrections and tightly scoped exceptions.

Organizations should treat MRP Live as the default candidate but assess coverage against their exact release and support package.

What should not be claimed without release-specific evidence

It is tempting to create a simple list saying, for example, “subcontracting was added in release X” or “stock transfer became supported in release Y.” In practice, these processes contain multiple variants:

  • Subcontracting at plant or subcontractor MRP-area level.
  • Stock transfer with single-level or multi-level source determination.
  • Schedule-line creation versus purchase-requisition creation.
  • Make-to-stock versus sales-order or project stock.
  • Standard processing versus customer enhancements.

A feature may have been partially supported before every variation was covered. The safer approach is to verify the exact scenario, release and Note implementation level.

Storage-Location Planning: A Key S/4HANA Functional Change

SAP S/4HANA 1511 removed the older concept of independently configured storage-location MRP. Instead, SAP positioned MRP areas as the standard model.

SAP Note 2268045 – S4TWL – Storage Location MRP states that S/4HANA plans at plant and MRP-area level. It explains that:

  • An MRP-area-specific type ND can exclude a location from planning.
  • An MRP-area-specific reorder-point type such as VB can represent separately planned replenishment.
  • MRP areas provide wider planning functionality than the former storage-location procedure.

The same Note recommends the migration report MRP_AREA_STORAGE_LOC_MIGRATION for conversions where the old model was detected.

Functional example

A manufacturing plant may have:

  • A production-supply location that should be planned independently.
  • A quality or hold location that should not generate replenishment.
  • A subcontractor location that must be planned separately.

The modern approach is to represent these as appropriate MRP areas and MRP-area-specific material settings, rather than assuming the historical storage-location MRP fields still drive planning.

How MRP Live Supports Common Supply-Chain Scenarios

1. In-house production

MRP Live compares finished-product demand with stock and receipts. If a shortage exists, it creates a planned order and generates dependent requirements for BOM components.

The quality of the result still depends on ordinary planning master data:

  • Procurement type.
  • Lot-sizing procedure.
  • In-house production time.
  • BOM validity.
  • Production version.
  • Safety stock.
  • Planning time fence.

Production versions are especially important because they connect the material to the usable BOM and routing or recipe.

2. External procurement

For a purchased component, the system can create a purchase requisition or relevant scheduling proposal based on procurement master data. Functionally, MRP Live is suitable for mainstream external procurement; unusual document-creation logic or custom enhancements must still be tested.

3. Plant-to-DC replenishment

In a multi-echelon network:

  1. A DC shortage creates a stock-transfer requirement.
  2. The supplying DC or plant sees that requirement as demand.
  3. Planning continues upstream until the manufacturing or purchasing source is reached.

This is where MRP Live’s ability to process a broad planning scope becomes valuable. However, reciprocal sourcing relationships, circular networks and custom supplying-plant logic still require careful job-design and end-to-end testing.

4. Subcontracting

A subcontracting scenario normally involves:

  • A value-added material received from a subcontractor.
  • Components provided to the subcontractor.
  • A subcontracting BOM.
  • Separate visibility of component stock at the subcontractor.

From the planner’s perspective, testing must confirm both sides: the procurement proposal for the subcontracted material and the component requirements to be provided to the vendor.

5. Mixed planning

Not every material must be processed identically. A planning run can contain:

  • Standard materials processed through MRP Live.
  • Selected materials explicitly assigned to classical processing.
  • Materials redirected because their scenario is unsupported in that installed release.
  • Materials affected by a release-specific correction.

An operational example documented for interchangeable MPN-MRP-set materials uses a Force Classic MRP setting and transaction MD_MRP_FORCE_CLASSIC to manage exceptions. This demonstrates why “MRP Live versus classical MRP” is not always an all-or-nothing decision.

MRP Live versus Classical MRP

Dimension

MRP Live

Classical MRP

Primary value

Faster, broader planning using SAP HANA and parallel processing.

Compatibility and predictable handling of established or exceptional scenarios.

Typical role

Strategic default for modern S/4HANA planning.

Selective fallback, forced-classic processing or transition safeguard.

Planning scope

Well suited to large plant, MRP-area and network-oriented runs.

Useful for individual materials, focused troubleshooting and older planning designs.

Planner experience

Closely aligned with current Fiori coverage, shortage monitoring and live planning results.

Familiar classic transactions and established result analysis.

Custom logic

Enhancements must be explicitly designed and tested for the MRP Live framework.

Existing classic MRP exits or BAdIs may continue to drive customer-specific results.

Legacy compatibility

Does not automatically preserve every historical enhancement or reporting dependency.

More suitable where a legacy enhancement is business-critical and has not been redesigned.

MRP lists

MRP Live is oriented toward current requirements data rather than creating the traditional stored MRP list. Custom reporting dependent on MRP lists may need redesign.

Can remain relevant where established processes still depend on classical planning outputs.

Recommended positioning

Default candidate, validated through scenario-based testing.

Exception engine—not necessarily the enterprise-wide default.

Historical Restrictions versus the 2025 Position

Historical restrictions

Early MRP Live releases had a smaller supported scope. Historical documentation may mention restrictions involving:

  • MRP areas.
  • Subcontracting.
  • Special procurement.
  • Sales-order or project-related planning.
  • Scheduling-agreement behavior.
  • Custom enhancement compatibility.
  • Interchangeable or manufacturer-part materials.

These references remain useful for understanding an old implementation, but they should not be copied into a 2025 design document without checking whether SAP later removed or corrected the restriction.

Scenarios where classical MRP can still be relevant in 2025

Classical processing may still be appropriate when:

  1. A material is explicitly forced to classical MRP.
  2. An SAP Note documents classic fallback for a particular scenario or release.
  3. Existing customer logic is implemented only in the classical enhancement framework.
  4. An interchangeable-material, supersession or MPN-MRP-set scenario produces different results.
  5. The organization needs a controlled workaround while an SAP correction is tested.
  6. Legacy reporting or interfaces depend on classical MRP outputs.
  7. A focused comparison run is required to investigate planning differences.

The business decision should be based on planning-result accuracy, not on a blanket belief that one engine is always superior.

 

Important SAP Notes and KBAs

SAP Notes are versioned and access-controlled. The latest Note version and software-component applicability should always be checked in SAP for Me before implementation.

Practical Recommendations

1. Build a planning-scenario inventory

Classify materials by:

  • In-house or external procurement.
  • Plant or MRP-area planning.
  • Stock transfer.
  • Subcontracting.
  • Sales-order or project stock.
  • Interchangeability or supersession.
  • Custom enhancement usage.

2. Test complete supply paths

Do not test only one material at one plant. Validate:

DC demand → supplying DC → hub → manufacturing plant → finished-good planned order → BOM components → purchase requisitions.

3. Compare results, not only runtime

Validate:

  • Quantities.
  • Dates.
  • Lot sizing.
  • Rescheduling messages.
  • Source of supply.
  • BOM explosion.
  • Subcontracting components.
  • Stock-transfer propagation.
  • Safety-stock behavior.

4. Separate standard coverage from custom behavior

A scenario can be standard-supported while a customer-specific BAdI or report remains incompatible with MRP Live.

5. Recheck historical restrictions after every upgrade

Maintain a release matrix with four statuses:

  • Supported in MRP Live.
  • Supported after SAP Note or support package.
  • Automatically processed through classical logic.
  • Intentionally forced to classical MRP.

Conclusion

MRP Live’s evolution from 1511 to 2025 is best understood as a gradual expansion of functional confidence.

It began as a HANA-optimized planning innovation with notable restrictions. Over time, SAP expanded coverage, strengthened MRP-area-oriented planning, improved planner tools and delivered corrections for increasingly specialized scenarios.

By 2025, the right question is no longer:

“Should we use MRP Live or classical MRP?”

The better question is:

“Which planning scenarios are fully supported by MRP Live in our exact release, and which exceptions still require classical logic, redesign or an SAP correction?”

For organizations with manufacturing plants, multiple DCs, stock-transfer networks and mixed procurement models, the strongest approach is therefore MRP Live by default, classical MRP by documented exception, and release-specific validation for every critical planning path.

entry.title: Re: PO Re-approval Release Strategy Trigger Failure on Qu...
entry.content:
The changeability is read from the release indicator the PO has at the moment of the change. After the final release that is the released indicator, not the blocked one, so a 6 on the blocked indicator does nothing for a released PO. I read the standard code that makes this decision (function module ME_REL_STRATEGIE_EKKO) and the release configuration tables in an S/4HANA 2023 system. This is how it works:

1. Which indicator counts

When a PO that already has a release is changed, the code reads the Release Indicator table (T16FB) with the indicator in EKKO-FRGKE. That is the indicator your Release statuses assign to the current status: the fully released one after the final release, or the one of a partial status. If it has changeability 2, the code stops there and the strategy is not determined again.

The system I checked has exactly this trap: the blocked indicator B has changeability 4 with a value tolerance of 10.0, but the release statuses give indicator G after the release, and G has changeability 2. With this setup a released PO never goes back for approval on a price change.

2. The value check (4 and 6)

With 4 or 6 on the current indicator, the code takes the old total value of the PO (CEKKO-GNETW, converted if the currency changed), adds the percentage from the "Value Change" field of that same indicator (TLFAE, "Tolerance for Value Changes During Release") and resets the release only if the new total is greater than the result:

  • A decrease never triggers a new release.
  • With 10.0 (10 percent) and an old total of 1000.00, a new total of 1100.00 does not trigger it, 1100.01 does.
  • With 0.0, any increase triggers it.
  • There is no separate check for quantity. A quantity change only counts through the total value, or if it leads to a different strategy.

3. What "outputted" adds in 5 and 6

If the PO was already output and the current indicator has anything other than 5 or 6, the code looks at the indicator the new status would get. If that one is not flagged as Released (field KZFRE), it keeps the old release values and the PO stays released. With 5 or 6 this step is skipped, so the new release also happens after output.

Two more rules in the same code: before the first release (EKKO-FRGZU empty) the strategy is simply determined again when the PO changes, and if a change leads to a different strategy, the release is reset with any changeability except 2.

What I would check in your system

  • A released PO that did not go back for approval: its EKKO-FRGKE before the change.
  • In Define Release Procedure for Purchase Orders, Release Indicator: changeability and "Value Change" of that indicator. That is where the 6 has to be.
  • In the Release statuses of the strategy: which indicator the fully released status gets.
  • The size of the change, against the old total plus the tolerance.

Not tested: I did not change a real PO. The system I used has no release class for purchasing documents (table T16FG is empty), so the function stops before the value check and I could not run it end to end. Everything above comes from the code and the configuration tables of that release. This is the classic release procedure: when the system type is S/4HANA Cloud, the same function clears the release data and exits.
